reviewFinding.summary: Avoid subnormal precision loss in the variance ratio

additionalReviewFindings.summary: Reject precision loss in subnormal geometric means
additionalReviewFindings.reason: An unequal-variance subnormal geometric scale cannot resolve the supplied correlation reliably.

additionalReviewFindings.summary: Detect perfect correlations caused by rounded geometric means
additionalReviewFindings.independentOracleMethod: 90-digit Python Decimal using Decimal.from_float for the exact binary covariance entry; 2e16 * (1 - covariance / sqrt(3)).
additionalReviewFindings.reason: For unequal variances near unit correlation, the implementation accepts perfect dependence only when Float roots reproduce both diagonals and their product exactly reproduces the covariance.

additionalReviewFindings.summary: Preserve rounding residuals when adjusting source contributions
additionalReviewFindings.independentOracleMethod: Exact rational residual from the binary64 inputs: (992800745259006 / 4503599627370497)^2, evaluated independently with Python Fraction.
additionalReviewFindings.actualResult: propagated covariance projection is numerically unresolved
additionalReviewFindings.reason: After power-of-two normalization, a near-zero Cholesky projection that contains any tolerated diagonal adjustment now returns an explicit unresolved error. This deliberately avoids inferring exact uniformity from rounded adjustment ratios.

additionalReviewFindings.summary: Verify exact uniformity before exempting adjusted cancellation
additionalReviewFindings.independentOracleMethod: Exact rational arithmetic over the exact binary Float inputs, evaluated independently with Python Fraction.
additionalReviewFindings.actualResult: propagated covariance projection is numerically unresolved
additionalReviewFindings.reason: The two rounded diagonal-adjustment ratios compare equal even though their exact ratios differ. Every near-zero projection with adjusted contributions now returns an explicit unresolved error; equal rounded factors no longer exempt cancellation.

additionalReviewFindings.summary: Do not treat rounded root squares as proof of exact dependence
additionalReviewFindings.independentOracleMethod: 100-digit Python Decimal using Decimal.from_float for the exact binary64 covariance entry and high precision sqrt(11).
additionalReviewFindings.reason: The rounded Float product sqrt(11) * sqrt(11) equals 11 without proving that the exact root square equals the supplied diagonal. Unequal-variance near-unit correlations are now certified only for small integer roots whose squares and cross product are exactly representable and equal the inputs; all other cases fail explicitly.

additionalReviewFindings.summary: Detect source adjustments hidden by rounded subnormal squares
additionalReviewFindings.independentOracleMethod: 100-digit Python Decimal from exact binary64 inputs: (sqrt(5e-324) * (1e16/sigmaA - 1e16/sigmaB))^2.
additionalReviewFindings.actualResult: propagated covariance projection is numerically unresolved
additionalReviewFindings.reason: Both distinct binary Float source sigmas square to the same subnormal Float, so comparing only rounded squares skipped adjustment and returned zero. Validation already accepts the roots within tolerance; propagation now preserves a root-space adjustment whenever sqrt(diagonal) differs exactly from the source sigma, even if the rounded squares compare equal.

additionalReviewFindings.summary: Reject lossy midpoints between unequal subnormal entries
additionalReviewFindings.reason: Halving the one-subnormal-unit difference rounds it to zero and selects one endpoint before correlation conversion. The implementation now divides each raw symmetric entry by the local geometric scale before averaging, so the correlation midpoint 0.375 is represented directly; the exact example changes from 2.5 to 2.75.

regression.oracle: independent Float64 calculation of covariance divided by the product of the two diagonal square roots

followupNumericalBoundary.reason: The geometric scale itself is subnormal and the source variances differ; its Float representation cannot resolve the correlation reliably.
followupNumericalBoundary.equalVarianceSubnormalBehavior: Equal subnormal diagonal variances use the diagonal as the exact geometric scale; the existing correlated cancellation regression remains accepted.

implementation.method: Use each diagonal directly when variances are equal; otherwise compute the geometric scale as sqrt(row variance) * sqrt(column variance), reusing validated standard deviations. Divide each raw off-diagonal entry by the local geometric scale before averaging in correlation space, preserving the variance implied by unequal subnormal entries without materializing an unrepresentable midpoint. The midpoint helper sums before halving whenever the sum is finite, so adjacent subnormal differences are not halved to zero; it halves first only on same-sign overflow. Apply accepted diagonal-adjustment ratios after exact power-of-two normalization. For subnormal variances, preserve a root-space adjustment whenever sqrt(covariance diagonal) differs from the source sigma even when the rounded squares compare equal. For unequal-variance near-unit correlations, accept exact dependence only for small integer roots whose squares and cross product are exactly representable and reproduce the supplied matrix. Accumulate Cholesky projections with compensation; reject every near-zero projection that contains adjusted contributions. Reject subnormal unequal-variance geometric scales and other unresolved correlations instead of erasing representable residual variance.
